faq.q: ### Is UAN mandatory for merging EPF accounts?
faq.a: Yes, a Universal Account Number (UAN) is mandatory. All your previous EPF accounts must be linked to your UAN for you to initiate an online transfer request.

faq.q: ### What if my previous employer is closed or unresponsive?
faq.a: If your previous employer is closed or unresponsive, you might face challenges. In such cases, you can try to get the 'Date of Exit' updated through your current employer or by submitting a physical application to the EPFO.

faq.q: ### Are there any tax implications when merging EPF accounts?
faq.a: No, merging EPF accounts is a transfer of funds from one account to another and does not attract any immediate tax liability. However, if any of your old accounts were inactive for a very long period (e.g., more than 5 years since resignation) and then withdrawn, tax implications might arise on the interest earned during the inactive period.

faq.q: ### How long does the EPF account transfer process usually take?
faq.a: The online transfer process typically takes anywhere from a few weeks to two months, depending on the promptness of approval from your previous and current employers and the EPFO processing time.

faq.q: ### Can I merge EPF accounts offline?
faq.a: Yes, you can still merge EPF accounts offline by submitting a physical Form 13 (Transfer Claim Form) to your current employer, who will then forward it to the EPFO for processing. However, the online method is generally faster and more convenient.

faq.q: ### What if my KYC details are not updated for my old EPF accounts?
faq.a: The KYC details need to be updated and verified for your UAN, not necessarily for each individual old EPF account. As long as your UAN has updated and verified KYC (Aadhaar, PAN, Bank Account), you should be able to initiate the transfer.

faq.q: ### What happens to the interest earned on old accounts during the transfer process?
faq.a: Interest continues to accrue on your old EPF accounts until the funds are successfully transferred to your new account. The entire accumulated balance, including interest, is transferred.
